=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- Requirement: "Issue-mode failure escalations are handed to the escalation judge without a stop notification or a human `/reclarify` wait." The PR description's Issue Mode section promises escalation stops go to the escalation judge (CLAUDE.md §28.G), not to a human with a `PushNotification`. The two `implement-issue-claude.md` files still carry the old text that says the opposite.
  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md` (line 3) and `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md` (line 3).
  Evidence of absence: Both files still read "Failures and ask-first operations still stop the project (§28.C). The ask then goes on the issue: one comment, the `ai:claude-blocked` label, and a `PushNotification`" at line 3. The PR did edit the parallel Issue Mode bullet in `implement-plan-claude.md` (line 117 of the twin) to add "An **escalation stop** is the exception ([Escalations](#escalations), CLAUDE.md §28.G): its comment starts `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 kind=escalation stop=<stop id> -->`, it sends no `PushNotification`, and instead of waiting for a human it hands the project checker the escalation wait." The matching sentence is missing from `implement-issue-claude.md`, so an issue-mode run reading that file instead of `implement-plan-claude.md` will follow the stale instruction, send a `PushNotification`, and stop waiting for a human, stalling the project. The fix is twin-first (Q40) to match the new §28.C/§28.G contract.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
